When the lines came out no one knew whether Luck was gonna play or not (Colts haven't said yet, but he's been practicing so good indication he will). Usually in situations like that when a game changing player is in doubt books open low knowing that if there's a dash on the favorite they can usually jack the lines up high enough to get balanced action on the dog, but if they open high, still see more action on the fav than the dog, and then later in the week it turns out the star player isn't playing it's r I suspect the books opened low wondering how much that would affect action they see. In a situation knowing that if they open low they can always raise them but if they opened incredibly high. They basically know they're not going to get titled action on the dog not getting many points simply because you don't bet a dog not getting big points. Now let's look at the other side, had they opened with a higher line. If the line opens higher an the book sees titled action on the fav, it's really hard for them to jack the line high enough to get action on the dog without jacking it so much there's an opportunity for a reverse rush by pointing the spread to a point where it's statistically just not likely to happen no matter how much better one team is than another. Over the long run almost fifty percent of NFL games are decided by seven points or less. Which on paper can be deceiving because that implies that fifty percent of games are decided by more than seven points. Which is true. but it doesn't factor in that over the long run the "Any given Sunday" effect comes into play. In the long run almost fifty percent of NFL games are won outright by teams that are by the numbers the dog, which drives the number of blowout wins by the fav way down. The other possibility is they open the line high and see tilted action on the dog, well when you start dropping points that a power house has to beat it's pretty easy to then get balanced action on them.

(Note: I'm drunk right now and just know those 50% stats from years of gambling, maybe I'll post sources tomorrow when I'm sober or maybe you just do your own google if you think I'm bullshitting.)

So the books put the lines where it is the easiest to adjust for unbalanced action, since in their ideal world they have the exact same amount of money on the fave and the dog and just rake their 10% juice eliminating any possibility of a losing game for them. Remember that lines aren't a predictor of hat they think will happen but how they can have the same amount of money on both sides of it. Then consider that early week gambling is mostly done by casuals (people who bet because, "Hey, that looks good.") and that casuals usually bet far less than players (gamblers who have some sort of "system" or "pattern" to maximize their winnings based on long term trends), or smarts (gamblers who absorb as much information about the game as they can before betting based solely on what they think will actually happen in that specific game without a "system" or regard or regard to long term trends) who will come in later in the week once injury reports & scouting have been done with much higher bankrolls to play. So they use the lower betters to adjust the line to where it is hopefully draws even action once the high stakes guys show up.

This line opened at 6.5 by the Vegas Modern Standard average meaning it's already gone up a point. It undoubtedly will go up more as the correction continues.
